description: Restructure the Epic detail page from a document page into a summary-first goal-status workbench: surface a single prominent lifecycle primary action with a touch-visible disabled reason, and reorder progress / current activity / next-issue-or-reason ahead of a demoted collapsible description with distinct advancement-status copy.

tasks.title: Single prominent lifecycle primary action with touch-visible disabled Mark Done reason
tasks.description: Introduce a pure selector `primaryLifecycleAction(status, readyToMarkDone)` encoding the spec matrix (idle→Start Epic, running→Pause, paused→Resume, ready & non-paused & non-terminal→Mark Done, paused-ready→Resume, done/closed→none) and render only that single prominent primary action in the header action row, replacing the current simultaneous Start/Pause/Resume buttons. Keep `Edit` and `Close Epic` as secondary outline actions. Always render `Mark Done` for every non-terminal epic: enabled when it is the primary, otherwise as a disabled secondary Button with an on-screen visible reason element (`data-testid="mark-done-disabled-reason"`) replacing the current `title` hover tooltip. Reason text: paused → resume-before-done copy; otherwise → unfinished linked-issue count copy. Invoking actions continues to call the existing useStartEpic/usePauseEpic/useResumeEpic/useMarkEpicDone hooks with TanStack Query invalidation on success.
acceptanceCriteria: Idle non-ready epic renders a single 'Start Epic' primary action and no Pause/Resume/Mark-Done primary; invoking it calls the start API.
Running non-ready epic renders a single 'Pause' primary action; invoking it opens the pause confirm flow and calls the pause API on confirm.
Paused epic renders 'Resume' as the primary action even when readyToMarkDone is true, and does NOT surface 'Mark Done' as the prominent primary.
Non-paused, non-terminal epic with readyToMarkDone=true renders 'Mark Done' as the prominent primary (replacing Start/Pause) and invoking it calls the mark-done API.
Done/Closed epic renders no Start/Pause/Resume/Mark Done lifecycle action.
When Mark Done is disabled (paused or unfinished remaining), a visible on-screen reason is rendered with `data-testid="mark-done-disabled-reason"` and the button carries no `title` attribute.
Disabled reason for a paused epic states the epic must be resumed before marking done.
Disabled reason for unfinished linked issues states the count of remaining unfinished linked issues (singular/plural).
Edit and Close Epic remain reachable and functional as secondary actions.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes.

`npm run test:run -w packages/web` passes, including new/updated cases in EpicDetailPage.test.tsx covering the primary-action matrix, the paused-ready Resume-primary case, the terminal no-action case, and the disabled-Mark-Done visible-reason cases (paused + unfinished).
Pure selector `primaryLifecycleAction` is unit-tested in isolation covering every cell of the (status × readyToMarkDone) matrix.
tasks.output: `packages/web/src/pages/epic-detail/model/primaryLifecycleAction.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) pure selector, updated header action row in `packages/web/src/pages/epic-detail/ui/EpicDetailPage.tsx` rendering the single prominent primary plus always-rendered Mark Done with visible disabled reason, and updated/added cases in `packages/web/src/pages/epic-detail/ui/EpicDetailPage.test.tsx`.
tasks.notes: Follow design decisions D3 (single prominent primary selector) and D4 (on-screen disabled reason, no title tooltip). The selector is a pure function placed under `pages/epic-detail/model/` mirroring the structure of `widgets/epic-dependency-graph/model/readiness.ts`. Do not render the status-based action that the primary replaces (e.g. no Pause button alongside a ready Mark Done primary). Mark Done remains rendered (disabled) when not primary so the disabled reason stays discoverable.

tasks.title: Summary-first information architecture with distinct advancement copy and collapsible description
tasks.description: Restructure EpicDetailPage into three regions: (1) Header Card whose first fold shows meta row + title + the prominent primary action (from T-001) followed by the existing 3-column summary grid (Progress / Next Issue / Current Activity), with the description removed from this card; (2) an Overview/Description card rendered only when `epic.description` is non-empty, after the summary, using `MarkdownReader mode="collapsible"`; (3) the unchanged Linked Issues card. Add a pure module `advancement.ts` that derives an `AdvancementState` discriminated union (running-but-idle, waiting-for-in-progress, draft-blocker, external-prerequisite-blocker, idle-no-next, has-next, nothing-pending) from `epic.linkedIssues` (mirroring `deriveReadiness` in readiness.ts — never by parsing `nextIssueReason`), and render the distinct advancement copy alongside the Next Issue column with navigation links to the relevant linked issue where one exists. Surface paused-epic pause reason + resume re-evaluation hint, idle-epic startable-next-or-why explanation, and ready-to-mark-done indication alongside the delivered/total counts. Preserve all existing detail capabilities (linked-issue list/edit/add, graph view, edit/close dialogs).
acceptanceCriteria: On desktop and at a 390px mobile viewport, the summary grid (progress, current activity, next issue/reason) appears in DOM and visual order before the Overview/Description region and is reachable in the first fold without scrolling past the full description.
Progress summary displays delivered/total counts (e.g. `2 / 5`); when readyToMarkDone is true it additionally surfaces a ready-to-mark-done indication.
Current Activity block lists active and blocked linked issues, each with a navigation link to that issue's detail page, and renders a clear empty state when there are none.
Next Issue block renders the startable next issue with a nav link when one exists; otherwise renders the advancement-state reason and never presents a non-existent issue as startable.

Advancement copy distinguishes each of: running-but-idle, waiting-for-in-progress (identifying the in-progress issue), draft-blocker, external-prerequisite-blocker, and nothing-pending — without collapsing them into a single generic message.
A running epic waiting on an in-progress linked issue renders a navigation link from the waiting reason to that issue's detail page.
Idle epic with a startable next issue shows that next issue with a nav link; idle epic with no startable next issue explains why without implying advancement.
Paused epic displays the pause reason and a hint that resuming will re-evaluate advancement (readiness + next startable issue).
Overview/Description region is rendered only when `epic.description` is non-empty; when empty, no Overview region is rendered.
Overview/Description region is collapsible via MarkdownReader's collapsible mode (exposes `markdown-collapse-control` / `markdown-expand-control` test hooks) and is placed after the summary.
Linked-issue listing, add-issue form, per-row start/remove, list/graph toggle, edit-epic dialog, and close-epic dialog remain present and functional.
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` passes.

`npm run test:run -w packages/web` passes, including new/updated cases in EpicDetailPage.test.tsx for summary-before-description DOM order (desktop + mobile), no-Overview-when-empty, collapsible Overview control, each advancement-state copy kind, paused reason + resume hint, and a no-regression check of linked-issue/edit/add capabilities.
Pure `advancement.ts` derivation is unit-tested in isolation asserting each `AdvancementState` kind and the navigation issue-number targets.
tasks.output: `packages/web/src/pages/epic-detail/model/advancement.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) pure AdvancementState derivation and copy table, restructured `packages/web/src/pages/epic-detail/ui/EpicDetailPage.tsx` (description moved into a collapsible Overview card after the summary grid; advancement copy wired into the Next Issue column; paused reason + resume hint surfaced), and updated/added cases in `packages/web/src/pages/epic-detail/ui/EpicDetailPage.test.tsx`.
tasks.notes: Follow design decisions D1 (client-side AdvancementState derivation, never parse nextIssueReason), D2 (three-region restructure keeping the max-w-4xl shell and Back to Epics link), and D5 (reuse CurrentActivityList/CurrentActivityEntry as-is; reuse MarkdownReader mode="collapsible" — do not build a new collapse primitive). The server-provided progress.nextIssue / nextIssueReason remain the source of truth for *what* the next issue is; the client derivation only enriches the *why* copy and nav targets and must not re-implement selection. Relies on prerequisite issue #277 (mobile horizontal-overflow fix) being done.
